technical-summary: Replaced the boolean remote flag on managed-config mechanisms with an explicit transports list. The old flag was modelled three different ways across three layers (a YAML boolean, a modifier per the loader docstring, and a one-element capability frozenset on ManagedConfigSpec) and conflated two distinct facts: whether the harness config format can express a url-form entry, and whether our registered reader/writer actually emit one. That conflation let goose declare remote support its stdio-only writer could not serialize, silently dropping urls, while eleven providers whose writers do emit url-form entries were left undeclared and routed to a stdio path. transports now states only what the adapter implements, defaults to [stdio], validates against KNOWN_TRANSPORTS with new code VAL-PCAP-012, and is surfaced through providers_api as transports. REMOTE_CAPABILITY is deleted. Added contract tests: default fallback, an assertion that every provider declaring http uses a writer that branches on is_remote, unknown-transport load failure, and a guard that no stale remote key survives.
user-summary-candidate: Replaced an ambiguous remote flag with an explicit transports declaration, fixing silently dropped remote MCP entries.

technical-summary: Gave the mcp capability kind its own mechanism schema instead of overloading the shared one. Added McpConfigSpec, registered as mcp-config-spec in MECHANISM_SCHEMA_MAP and referenced by the mcp kind in _capabilities.yaml; ManagedConfigSpec is domain-neutral again, so hooks, lsp-config, plugins and models no longer carry a transports field that has no meaning for them. transports is now required with no default: an omitted declaration raises VAL-PCAP-012 rather than silently asserting stdio support, which was the same absence-implies-capability defect that left eleven adapters misdeclared under the old boolean. Codex now declares transports [stdio] explicitly. providers_api emits transports only for specs that carry it. Regenerated capability-id-taxonomy.md via its generator. Tests assert every mcp adapter declares transports, that domain-neutral kinds carry none, that a missing declaration is a load error, and that any adapter claiming http uses a writer branching on is_remote.
user-summary-candidate: Moved MCP transport declarations into their own schema and made them explicit rather than assumed.

technical-summary: Taught the Goose provider adapter Goose native remote extension format so Goose reaches Hindsight through the shared remote MCP recipe like every other MCP provider. The adapter previously treated the extensions block as a list when Goose documents a mapping keyed by name, meaning read_goose_yaml would have called .get() on a string against a real Goose config, and it hardcoded type stdio with cmd/args so any url-form entry silently lost its endpoint. Remote entries now serialize as type streamable_http with uri and headers, sse is read-tolerated but never written, the legacy list shape is still readable because earlier versions of this module wrote it into user configs, and unrelated extensions and top-level settings are preserved. goose.yaml declares transports stdio and http. No Hindsight knowledge entered the adapter and no harness knowledge entered Hindsight: audited all nine recipes and confirmed every path targets ~/.hindsight/ while every harness-side change goes through a provider step. Replaced an earlier source-grep guard with a behavioural round-trip test asserting a remote entry survives write-then-read through every http-declaring provider adapter; the grep version had produced a false failure once the is_remote branch moved into a helper. All twenty providers now route correctly and nothing resolves to the stdio recipe.
user-summary-candidate: Goose now gets Hindsight through the standard remote MCP route instead of a broken stdio path.

technical-summary: Replaced the generic MCP remote capability flag with a typed, required transport declaration on McpConfigSpec; validated and serialized transport metadata; updated provider descriptors and Hindsight routing; corrected Goose MCP mapping/HTTP round-tripping; and completed HM22 with focused behavioral coverage.
user-summary-candidate: Completed the MCP transport refactor and HM22: provider adapters now declare and preserve stdio/HTTP entry shapes, Goose remote MCP round-trips correctly, and Hindsight routes through the standard remote recipe.
